guides.title: Corsair Visual Instrument · Connection
guides.description: Use Connection in Corsair Visual Instrument.
guides.before_you_start: Keep your existing values for a read-only tour. Opening this guide does not activate a provider, start services or apply settings.
learning_outcomes: Establish one SDK connection in iCUE

steps.title: Establish one SDK connection in iCUE
steps.body: Keep iCUE running and read Keyboard discovery for Device Memory Mode and allow-SDK settings. If the SDK is not available, the addon cannot drive lighting. In Connection click Reconnect & Rescan once, then read Connection status and Status detail. A successful SDK connection is required before designing effects.

steps.title: Read status before changing renderers
steps.body: Connection status and Status detail name the actual SDK or device problem. If the link fails, follow that reason and rescan before touching Devices or Advanced SDK. Renderer overrides and previews are not evidence of a healthy connection.

steps.title: Check which keyboard will receive the effect
steps.body: Open Devices and read Detected keyboards. Leave Force zone renderer and Force per-key renderer on Automatic by LED layout for a first test. Locate your physical keyboard and note any offline warning. If absent or offline, wake it in iCUE and use Reconnect & Rescan.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Force a renderer only for a detected layout problem
steps.body: Automatic can drive every supported discovered keyboard, so record all listed devices. Force a zone or per-key renderer only when a working connection shows a detected layout that needs correction. A forced renderer does not fix an SDK connection error.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

guides.title: Corsair Visual Instrument · State colors & mood
guides.description: Use State colors & mood in Corsair Visual Instrument.
guides.before_you_start: Keep your existing values for a read-only tour. Opening this guide does not activate a provider, start services or apply settings.
learning_outcomes: A swatch is configuration, not output

steps.title: Choose four distinct base colors
steps.body: Choose clearly different Idle, Listening, Thinking and Speaking swatches. A Text Only chat will not exercise Listening. For a first design use a quiet Idle and bright Speaking color. Leave Tint state colors with the current mood off so the base colors stay easy to tell apart.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: A swatch is configuration, not output
steps.body: Changing and saving four swatches does not prove the keyboard shows them. The animation designer preview and a real spoken reply provide that evidence. If the colors become hard to distinguish, return to simple hues before enabling mood tint.

guides.title: Corsair Visual Instrument · Keyboard animation designer
guides.description: Use Keyboard animation designer in Corsair Visual Instrument.
guides.before_you_start: Keep your existing values for a read-only tour. Opening this guide does not activate a provider, start services or apply settings.
learning_outcomes: Send your first Speaking hardware preview

steps.title: Send your first Speaking hardware preview
steps.body: Set State to edit to Speaking and choose one Animation. Speed controls movement, Intensity its strength, Animation size its extent and Trail / softness how long it fades. Change one value at a time while watching Keyboard preview, then use Preview Speaking and watch the physical keys. Test audio level supplies preview energy; it does not record your microphone.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Separate on-screen preview from hardware output
steps.body: If Keyboard preview changes but hardware does not, revisit Connection status and Detected keyboards. A working hardware preview proves the lighting path; it does not prove runtime speech animation, which the next Speech response exercise checks separately.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

guides.before_you_start: Keep your existing values for a read-only tour. Opening this guide does not activate a provider, start services or apply settings.

steps.title: Compare preview energy with a real spoken reply
steps.body: Speech sensitivity scales outgoing playback energy and Speech smoothing softens rapid changes; neither changes microphone recognition. Keep your preview values, then ask one short Main Chat question with the runtime ON and a working TTS provider. Watch for Speaking during audible output. Raise sensitivity slightly if motion is faint; add smoothing if it flickers.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Use volume controls when the effect is too strong
steps.body: If the whole effect is overpowering, lower Brightness under Global output rather than changing microphone settings. Use Sensitivity and Smoothing for motion character only. If chat produces no response, confirm actual spoken playback before adjusting the speech response values.

guides.before_you_start: Keep your existing values for a read-only tour. Opening this guide does not activate a provider, start services or apply settings.
learning_outcomes: Choose the startup state, then close the loop

steps.title: Bound the output for comfort
steps.body: Brightness sets the overall light level, Animation speed scales movement, and Frame cap limits updates per second. Lower Brightness first if distracting, then reduce Frame cap and confirm motion is still readable. These values apply to every runtime state.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Choose the startup state, then close the loop
steps.body: Review Enable Corsair visual lighting at startup for the next NC session; changing it does not toggle current lighting. You are done when both a hardware preview and a real spoken reply produced expected lights. If only the preview worked, keep troubleshooting runtime speech.

steps.title: Read the required SDK before browsing
steps.body: Advanced SDK shows the 64-bit SDK DLL path; a DLL is the library that lets NC talk to iCUE, not an effect file. If the preview worked, leave it alone. Use Connection status and Status detail to identify a missing or incompatible SDK before choosing Browse for SDK DLL.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Change the SDK path only with a record to restore
steps.body: Record the existing path first. If notes call for a change, use Browse for SDK DLL to select the 64-bit library, then Reconnect & Rescan. If connection worsens, restore the recorded path and rescan. Do not use renderer overrides to hide an SDK error.
